page.layout: One printed page of running text in a single column, with marginal notes in the left margin (verse references and one note on "Armatus"). The running head and page number are at the top. The right edge shows part of the neighbouring page, which is not transcribed.

main_text.p: terpretari abundantiam; supra autem cap. 41. vers. 34. vertisse justitiam. At nulla mirandi causa est, cùm non eadem utrobique sit dictio. Hic enim est abundantia, saturitas; illic autem quod & septem significat, & juramentum. Ver. 34. Et quintam abit terram Ægypti.] Id est, ut eam ponit Aben Ezra, quintam partem terrae possidebit. Ita etiam Jonathan, Faciet Pharao & constituet procuratores super terram, qui accipiant quintam partem ex quinque, id est quintam partem ex omni frumento terrae Ægypti. Similia habet & Targum Hierosolymitanum. Onkelos autem interpretatur armet, vel armatus, quemadmodum (quod notat R. Salom. qui etiam huic expositioni consensit) armator significat. Sed prior interpretatio est simplicior, idque Mercerus magis probat, ut hic quemadmodum cap. 47. a 4. quintatio significetur. LXX, καὶ ἀπὸ τῶν πέντε... & deponant quintam partem omnium frugum terrae Ægypti. Vulg. Et quintam partem frugum terrae Ægypti, &c.

Armare (inquit Fagius) metaphoricè accipit pro prospicere, providere. Ver. 40. Et juxta os tuum (sen ex mandato tuo) gubernabitur omnis populus meus.] Vel, armabitur. Sic Fagius vertit in Collat. at in Chald. Paraph. ait sensum à Paraphraste expressum esse simplicissimum, nempe juxta verbum (sen mandatum) tuum cibabitur omnis populus meus. Ità etiam Jonath. juxta decretum verbi tui cibabitur omnis populus meus. Similiter R. Sal. interpretatur, cibabitur, sustentabitur

page.notes: The page is heavily blurred and show-through from the reverse side is present. Hebrew and Greek words are only partly legible and may contain errors. The Greek and Hebrew passages were transcribed as far as they could be read; the Hebrew after "Similiter R. Sal." is largely illegible. The verse references in the left margin are faint. The note "Ver. 39." near the foot of the left margin is barely visible and is not transcribed. The final word of the page, "sustentabitur", is cut off by the lower edge of the column and is read conservatively.
